name: Ivan Kowalski

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: I work for the Work Futures Panel. We have no ties to AI firms, employers, unions, parties or government; we sell nothing and campaign for no side. Your answers are confidential. What does a shift involve?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: I lead the evening complaints team at a contact centre. I take the calls nobody can settle, check the written decisions and help newer agents keep their heads when a customer shouts. My two-year college diploma got me started, but fifteen years of doing this made me good at it. The lead rate is still low for this job.

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: What is waiting when you get home?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: My wife Mara works at a school kitchen, and our two children are nine and thirteen. The mortgage is paid from both wages, with less than one month of expenses saved. There are only a couple of similar centres nearby. I sometimes use the approved AI search after the day team has tested an answer, but I still read the account myself.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AI Plateau: Picture this. AI turns out to be mostly hype. It automates some routine tasks and saves a bit of time here and there, but nothing radical changes. Jobs, pay and prices carry on much as they would have anyway.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell my team the new search saves a little time, but we still own a wrong refund. A tool cannot explain to a parent why the parcel fee was charged twice.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Quietly, I would be relieved about the work and still worried about money. My lead badge sounds senior, but the pay is low and our reserve would not cover a whole mortgage month.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Now I will keep handling the escalated refund calls and make agents check the live account before using an AI answer. In the first year I will put the small overtime payments into the mortgage account instead of replacing our dining table.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel uneasy when I think about the bank balance, even in a quiet technology year. Keeping the same shifts is welcome, but one missed payment would hurt.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Who checks the disputed refunds now?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I check the account history and sign the final correction. My colleague Saira checks the next shift handover, so a customer does not start the whole story again.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Why the table?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The table wobbles, but the children can do homework on it. A new one would take most of what our overtime earned this month.

do: Keep taking **refund escalations** and checking live accounts.
Put **overtime pay** toward the mortgage instead of buying a new table.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Steady Disruption: Now picture this. AI brings strong change, but not a revolution. Over the next few years it takes over many thinking tasks in many jobs: writing, checking, planning, buying, booking, coding and answering customers. Robots spread into hands-on work more slowly. Some jobs shrink, new ones appear, and lots of people have to change how they work. Most people still have work, and there is some time to adjust.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell the floor to count the reopened complaints, not just how many chats the software closes. If easy calls vanish, the hard cases need time and a sensible target.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I expect fewer paid evening hours even if I am the last person who can fix a bill. The school kitchen wage alone cannot cover our mortgage, and there are few centres to move to.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: This month I will use the approved checker on twenty closed refund cases with Saira and log every wrong amount. We will take the count to our manager together and ask for a target that includes corrections. If my rota is cut in the first year, I will apply for a posted paid complaints role only after I see written wages and hours that cover the mortgage.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I am anxious about hours, not frightened of the button itself. Knowing the errors gives us something useful to say.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Will you learn a different tool?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: If this checker becomes part of my job, I will ask Saira to show me the report view on paid time. I will practise on closed cases before using it on a live customer.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you leave for a better title?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: No. I would compare a full weekly rota and the written rate, then check Mara can still collect the children on my late days. A title without enough paid hours cannot pay our bank.

Apply after rota cuts only for **posted paid roles** with written mortgage-covering wages, hours and workable pickup.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2028: Next one. The singularity hits fast. Within 2 years, by 2028, there is full AGI: artificial general intelligence, meaning AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do, as well or better, and cheaper. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2031. It arrives before most companies, governments and families have time to prepare.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell the evening team that full thinking AI by 2028 could settle nearly every call we take. Hands-on robots around 2031 do not give a phone desk extra time.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I expect the centre to cut my team and perhaps my own post. With less than a month saved, I cannot wait for another centre to open; Mara cannot pay our mortgage alone.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Now I will ask for written dates for any rota cuts and freeze our plan to replace the dining table. If the post ends in the first year after 2028, I will apply for posted paid building reception work only when its written wages and hours cover the mortgage and the children's pickup; I will not resign on a rumour.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I am alarmed. Two years is short when a family has less than a month in reserve.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Why building reception?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I have handled visitors at our centre when the front desk is short, but that does not make me a building manager. I would ask what a paid reception shift really includes before I claim I can do it.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you buy a new qualification?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Only if a real posted job requires it and the employer pays the fee and time. I cannot put a course on a card while the mortgage is due.

do: Request **written cut dates** and defer the dining table.

steps.text: Delay replacing the dining table while the current one remains usable

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2031: Now the same thing, a bit slower. Full AGI arrives within 5 years, by 2031: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2034. There are a few years to see it coming, but it's still fast.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would say five years gives us time to inspect real jobs, but our calls still face full AGI by 2031. Hands-on robots arriving around 2034 may change a building desk later.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I might keep leading complaints for a few years while I find a real reception route. I do not believe a certificate on its own is a wage, especially with our savings so low.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: This year I will keep the evening shift and ask a local building about a supervised paid reception day if it posts a place. If it posts a paid vacancy with wages and hours covering our mortgage and pickup and funds a required safety course on paid time, I will complete it. In the first year after 2031 I will move only with a written offer meeting those terms.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I am anxious, but the extra years let me see the actual shift. I cannot gamble a mortgage on a course brochure.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would a trial day tell you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would see whether the early opening and visitor checks fit our school routine. If the trial is unpaid, I cannot treat it as an income route.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What if no place appears?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would keep my current paid shift while it exists and ask for written notice if hours change. I will not leave for a building job that exists only in a conversation.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2036: Last one. Full AGI arrives within 10 years, by 2036: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2039. It's the same end point, but there's about a decade to prepare, change careers and make plans.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell agents that ten years lets us compare real paid routes while the calls still bring wages. General AI reaches our desks by 2036 and hands-on robots around 2039.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: At 53 I may still owe on the mortgage, though our children should need less collecting. I would rather build a reserve than announce a new career before seeing a vacancy.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: This year I will keep leading the evening team and save the small overtime payments toward three months of expenses. I will check posted building reception roles each year. In the first year after 2036, if my call hours fall, I will move only on a written paid offer with wages and hours covering the mortgage; I will check the family rota before giving notice.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel uneasy about the end of the decade, but reasonably steady this year. More time helps only if I use the wages to build breathing room.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Why only three months?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Three months would be a big improvement from under one. If our hours fall, the target moves back; I will not borrow to call it savings.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you take a lower-paid shift for stability?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would calculate the full week first, including travel and the mortgage. Mara and I need both wages until the loan is manageable.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Of the five pictures, which one worries you most, and what would actually help you if it happened?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: AGI by 2028 worries me most. I could lose a team and a wage before we save even one mortgage month. Written notice and a posted paid job with hours we can live on would help.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Is there anything I didn't ask that I should have?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: Ask who signs the correction when an automated refund is wrong. I can count errors, but somebody must have paid time to fix them. A fast close is not a settled complaint.

headlineQuote: A fast close is not a settled complaint.
portrait: Ivan is a **43-year-old team lead** with a two-year diploma and strong complaints skill.
His **low lead pay**, mortgage, children and less than one month saved make lost hours urgent.
He uses **approved AI occasionally** after coworkers test it, and few similar jobs are nearby.
He checks **written wages and hours**, paid training and school pickup before changing work.
biggestWorry: **AGI by 2028** could remove both his team and household wage before he builds a reserve.
whatWouldHelp: **Written notice** and posted paid work with mortgage-covering hours would help.
